english.title: Obtain services dishonestly - Fraud Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) obtained services, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SERVICES..), for

(A)_[yourself]_
(B)_[another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..),]_

by a dishonest act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), those services having been made available on the basis that payment had been, was being or would be made for or in respect of them, and you obtained them without any payment having been made for or in respect of them or without payment having been made in full, and when you did so you knew that they were being or might be made available on that basis, but you intended that payment would not be made, or would not be made in full

english.notes:
See H9071 and H9075 respectively for the " attempt " and " conspiracy " variations of this Standard Offence Wording document.

(i) It is not possible to commit the offence by omission alone and it can be committed only where the dishonest act was done with intent not to pay for the services as expected.
(ii) This offence replaces the offence of obtaining services by deception in section 1 of the Theft Act 1978, though the new offence contains no deception element.
(iii) The offence is not inchoate; it requires the actual obtaining of the service. For example, data or software may be made available on the internet to a certain category of person who has paid for access rights to that service. A person dishonestly using false credit card details or other false personal information to obtain the service would be committing the offence. It would also cover the situation where a person climbs over a wall and watches a football match without paying the entrance fee. Such a person is not deceiving the provider of the service directly, but is obtaining a service which is provided on the basis that people will pay for it. Another example is where a person attaches a decoder to his television to enable viewing access to cable or satellite television channels for which he has no intention of paying.
(iv) Section 12 of the Act makes provision for directors, managers, secretaries or other similar officers or person purporting to act in such a capacity to be liable to prosecution where a body corporate has committed this offence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

For offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty is six months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
